//: Configuration for Codacy's Biome tool ONLY.
This repository does not use Biome. ESLint is the local linter (web/eslint.config.js
for web/, eslint.config.mjs for everything else) and Biome appears here solely because
Codacy runs it as one of its analysers.
WHY THE QWIK RULES ARE OFF:
Codacy's Biome tool has four `useQwik*` patterns enabled by the Default coding
standard, which cannot be disabled per pattern, and Codacy exposes no per-rule
parameter for the tool (codacy tool --help: enable | disable | configuration-file).
Those rules implement Qwik's $() serialisation boundary, and this project has no Qwik
dependency at all — `grep -i qwik package.json web/package.json` is empty. So they fire
on ordinary TypeScript: PR #222 was blocked by
`Biome lint/correctness/useQwikValidLexicalScope` on a plain arrow function in a
Playwright spec. A framework rule set pointed at a project that does not use that
framework is an analyser misconfiguration, not a finding.
WHAT ELSE IS OFF, AND WHY:
noDoubleEquals, noGlobalIsNan, noSwitchDeclarations and useBlockStatements are
stylistic and already governed locally by ESLint; Biome's opinion is not this repo's
and it was not requested. The security rules are deliberately left ON — they agree with
eslint-plugin-security, which the local configs now run (harness L-017), so a finding
from either analyser is a real finding.
IF YOU EDIT THIS: verify it the only way that works — push, then read
codacy -o json pull-request gh d-o-hub rust-ascii-canvas <PR>
A Biome config change has no local oracle; Biome is not installed here and must not
become a project dependency for a tool the repo does not use.
